solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Tie in school ultimately non-negotiable (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: what comes ultimately comes at the end, so take the final letter

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
the last letter of non-negotiable

annotation.surface: A school rule that no tie may be left off, and no arguing about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like the knotted thing round a pupil's neck; it is a match, as in a cup tie. GAM is an old whaling word for a school of whales.
annotation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a single game between two teams.

entries.clue: Astounded work supported kinky sex breaks (10)

indicatorNotes.supported: in a down clue what is supported sits on top, so GO comes above BACKED
indicatorNotes.breaks: S&M breaks into BACKED, splitting it open

blocks.note: a machine that goes is working
to back is to support; S&M goes in after the B
S&M, sadomasochism

annotation.surface: Someone astonished at kinky sex going on in the office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'supported' does two jobs: it gives a word and, in a down clue, says what sits on top of it. Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly amazed.
annotation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is informal British for astounded, as if struck in the mouth.

entries.clue: Still in need of a poet laureate? (10)

blocks.note: Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009
a thing that is -less is lacking, so in need of it

annotation.surface: Is the country still waiting for someone to fill the laureate's post?
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'Still' as 'even now' and the clue is a question about a vacancy; it is the adjective. The Poet Laureate is the UK's official court poet.
annotation.definitionFit: Motionless and still both describe something not moving.

entries.clue: Taken aback, coughed up Chinese university society fine (10)

indicatorNotes.Taken aback: taken back to front, so PAID runs the other way

blocks.note: to cough up is to pay, reluctantly
the Han are China's majority people
the Open University
S is the standard abbreviation for society

annotation.surface: Someone startled at having to pay a fine to a Chinese university society.
annotation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as a penalty at the end of the story; it is the definition, meaning delicate. 'Taken aback' looks like surprise and only turns PAID round.
annotation.definitionFit: Diaphanous fabric is fine enough to see through.

entries.clue: Irish serviceman not meeting expected standards (9)

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
a regular is a professional soldier

annotation.surface: An Irish soldier who falls short on the parade ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is that the regular soldier becomes his own opposite once the Irish tag goes in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Something irregular breaks the rules or falls below the usual standard.

entries.clue: Extra payment put up to secure very large venture (5)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.to secure: PIT holds OS fast inside it

blocks.note: a tip is paid on top of the bill
OS = outsize, a clothing label

annotation.surface: A bonus raised to fund a big business venture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'venture' looks like a business project; here it is the verb, as in venturing an opinion.
annotation.definitionFit: To posit a theory is to venture it, putting it forward for discussion.

entries.clue: Preoccupied men in debt with sad careers (6-6)

indicatorNotes.careers: to career is to rush about wildly, so the letters are thrown around

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram fodder, 3 letters

annotation.surface: Men in debt, with dismal jobs, whose minds are elsewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'careers' reads as a plural noun, jobs; it is the verb, to rush about out of control.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone preoccupied is absent-minded, thinking of other things.

entries.clue: Miss Cambridge University’s past love (4)

indicatorNotes.past: MIT has gone past love, so O is left in front

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, and nil looks like O
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

annotation.surface: A young woman at Cambridge recalling an old flame.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambridge points at England and at 'Miss' as a student; it is the Cambridge in Massachusetts, home of MIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: missing out a word or a name from a list means leaving it out.

entries.clue: Losses sustained periodically in Seattle gorge (4)

indicatorNotes.Losses sustained periodically in: Seattle loses a letter at regular intervals, keeping every other one

blocks.note: S-e-A-t-T-l-E: the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters

annotation.surface: A report of losses suffered now and then in a canyon near Seattle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine; it is the verb, to eat one's fill.
annotation.definitionFit: To sate yourself is to gorge until full.

entries.clue: Extra time fills fraction of device’s memory (4)

indicatorNotes.fills: T goes inside BYE, filling it

blocks.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the batter hitting the ball
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: Extra time taking up part of a gadget's memory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extra time' reads as one phrase from football; split it, and 'Extra' is the cricket BYE.
annotation.definitionFit: A byte is eight bits, a small unit of computer memory.

entries.clue: Doctor and sister starting round quietly in formal attire (5,5)

indicatorNotes.starting: letters that start jump about, so SISTER is jumbled
indicatorNotes.round: the jumbled SISTER goes round SH

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
SISTER jumbled, split ESS...IRT around SH
sh! means be quiet

annotation.surface: A doctor and a nurse doing their rounds quietly in evening dress.
annotation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse, so doctor and sister on a ward round is a real scene; 'starting' and 'round' are both instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: A dress shirt is the stiff white shirt worn with a dinner jacket.

entries.clue: Unusually tall iceberg a geographical phenomenon (7,5)

indicatorNotes.Unusually: the letters are arranged in an unusual order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A remarkably tall iceberg as a natural wonder.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' that looks like it belongs to the definition is the last letter of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A glacier table is a boulder left standing on a pillar of ice, a landform of glaciers.

entries.clue: Employed outside job fair displaying seat covers (12)

indicatorNotes.covers: MOONING goes round LIGHT, covering it

blocks.note: to moon is to show one's bare bottom; LIGHT goes after MOON
fair hair is light hair

annotation.surface: A fair-goer with a second job putting covers on seats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'seat' here is the backside, and mooning is baring it. 'Employed outside job' means doing work on top of your main job.
annotation.definitionFit: Moonlighting is holding a second job, usually in secret, outside one's main one.

entries.clue: Couple in middle of Gretna wearing wreathes, madly in love (10)

indicatorNotes.Couple in middle of: take the pair of letters at the centre of Gretna
indicatorNotes.wearing: the anagram of WREATHES wears ET, carrying it inside
indicatorNotes.madly: the letters of WREATHES are shaken up wildly

blocks.note: WREATHES jumbled, split SWE...HEART around ET
GR-ET-NA: the two central letters

annotation.surface: A couple at Gretna Green in garlands, madly in love.
annotation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, is where eloping English couples famously married. 'love' is a term of endearment, as in 'hello, love'.
annotation.definitionFit: Sweetheart and love are both fond names for someone dear.

entries.clue: Running low on salt? (10)

blocks.note: the surface wants 'running low' as nearly used up; the setter means flowing, as a river does
not a kitchen short of seasoning but water with little salt in it, unlike the sea

annotation.surface: Someone whose salt cellar is nearly empty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Running low' reads as nearly used up; read it as flowing water with little salt in it, like a river.
annotation.definitionFit: Fresh water, as in rivers, flows and has low salt content.

entries.clue: Stomach pains pass if caught in the earliest stages (5)

indicatorNotes.in the earliest stages: only the first stage of each word is used, its opening letter

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass

blocks.clueFragment: if caught in the earliest stages
blocks.note: the first letters of if and caught

annotation.surface: Medical advice: stomach pains will pass if spotted early.
annotation.walkthrough: 'pass' reads as the verb, the pains going away; it is the noun, a gap between mountains.
annotation.definitionFit: Colic is severe, spasmodic pain in the abdomen.

entries.clue: Spooner’s keen for cow as grass management aid (9)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of two words

blocks.note: to keen is to wail in mourning; MOURN gives up its M for an L
a cow lows, so it is a lower; it takes the M in exchange

annotation.surface: Spooner suggesting a cow as a way of keeping the grass down.
annotation.walkthrough: Say 'mourn lower' aloud and swap the M and L. A cow is a lower because it lows, or moos; the joke is that a grazing cow really does keep grass short.
annotation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is the machine used to keep grass cut.

entries.clue: Fell apart, as one at the wheel did? (4,2,3)

annotation.definition2: as one at the wheel did?

blocks.note: to go to pot is to go to ruin

blocks.clueFragment: as one at the wheel did?
blocks.note: a potter at the wheel literally goes to work on a pot

annotation.surface: A driver who went to pieces behind the wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: The wheel looks like a car's; it is a potter's wheel, where the clay is made into a pot.
annotation.definitionFit: To go to pot is to deteriorate or fall to pieces.

entries.clue: Singer, in need of opening, rehearsed new moves (2,7)

indicatorNotes.in need of opening: the word is missing its opening letter
indicatorNotes.moves: the letters move about into a new order

blocks.note: REHEARSED without its first letter R
N is the abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: A singer who, needing an opener, practised some new dance moves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'opening' sounds like a gig's support slot; it is the first letter of 'rehearsed'. Ed Sheeran is an English singer-songwriter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular English pop singer-songwriter stands for the general word.

entries.clue: Vegetables once known as “hollow potatoes” (5)

indicatorNotes.hollow: a hollow word has its inside taken out, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: née introduces a woman's former, maiden name
P...S, the outer letters of potatoes

annotation.surface: A trivia fact: these vegetables used to be called hollow potatoes.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a real old name; they only fence off the wordplay. Neeps is Scots for turnips or swedes, eaten with haggis.
annotation.definitionFit: Neeps are turnips or swedes, a Scottish word for the vegetables.

entries.clue: Obscure athletes who succeeded attract most attention (5,3,4)

indicatorNotes.Obscure: the letters are obscured, jumbled out of recognition

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

annotation.surface: Unknown athletes who won and grabbed the headlines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective, little-known; it is the instruction to jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: To steal the show is to draw the most attention away from everyone else.

entries.clue: Advantage of a screen in the auditorium (5)

indicatorNotes.in the auditorium: an auditorium is where things are heard

blocks.note: a veil screens the face

annotation.surface: The benefit of having a screen in a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The auditorium suggests a cinema screen; the screen here is a veil.
annotation.definitionFit: Avail means use or benefit, as in 'to no avail'.

entries.clue: Typically dusty passageway, glad I took masks (4)

indicatorNotes.masks: the words mask the answer, hiding it inside

blocks.note: four letters run across the join, from the end of the first word to the start of the third

annotation.surface: Someone relieved they wore a mask in a dusty tunnel.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a real mine-safety story, which is why masks sounds like face-masks rather than hiding.
annotation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine, usually dusty.

entries.clue: Religious festival widely celebrated by mothers (4)

blocks.note: by = times, as in four by four, written x
ma is mother, so mas are mothers

annotation.surface: A festival mothers everywhere keep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like the passive 'celebrated by'; it is the multiplication sign X.
annotation.definitionFit: Xmas is the short written form of Christmas, a widely kept Christian festival.

entries.clue: Carefree on leaving show, one of seven heading for better parts (5-5)

indicatorNotes.heading for: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a demo shows how something works
the first letter of better
Happy is one of the Seven Dwarfs in Snow White

annotation.surface: A dwarf leaving a show in high spirits, bound for better parts.
annotation.walkthrough: Demob is British for demobilisation, release from the armed forces; demob-happy is the giddy mood of someone about to leave a job or the army.
annotation.definitionFit: Demob-happy describes the carefree mood of someone about to be released.

entries.clue: Great chunk of retirement savings withdrawn (4)

indicatorNotes.chunk of: only a chunk of the words is used, a run of letters inside them
indicatorNotes.withdrawn: drawn back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: retiremen-T SAV-ings, read backwards

annotation.surface: A large sum taken out of a pension pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' is money taken out of an account in the surface; here it reverses the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Vast and great both mean very large.

entries.clue: Two girls, terrible enemies at first, are a perfect fit for each other (10)

annotation.definition: are a perfect fit for each other

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: TESS and ELLA, two girls' names
the first letters of terrible and enemies

annotation.surface: Two girls who hated each other at first turn out to be perfectly matched.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a friendship story; the definition is about shapes, like tiles, fitting together with no gaps.
annotation.definitionFit: Shapes that tessellate fit together perfectly, covering a surface without gaps.

entries.clue: Move segment of flight to avoid America (4)

indicatorNotes.to avoid: the word avoids A, leaving it out

blocks.note: one stair is a single step in a flight of stairs; drop its A
A is the abbreviation for America

annotation.surface: Rerouting part of an air journey so it misses the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'flight' reads as a plane journey; it is a flight of stairs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs cover the smallest shift, as when someone sleeping first shows signs of life.
